headline: Applied AI Field Engineer & Software Developer
summary: Software developer with 12+ years of experience building full-stack applications and enterprise systems. As an Applied AI Field Engineer at Trilon Group, I conduct onsite deep dives with engineering firms and rapidly turn complex workflows into working software: deterministic calculation and document-processing tools, human-in-the-loop AI workflows, and the data architecture underneath them.
bio: I’m Shane Miller, a software engineer based in Boulder, Colorado, with over a decade in complex production environments — global financial data platforms, core banking systems, and products I’ve built and shipped myself.

Right now I’m an Applied AI Field Engineer at Trilon Group. I work with a cross-functional team doing onsite deep dives with engineering firms — documenting how the work actually gets done, then building software for the parts worth automating. Mostly deterministic calculation and document tools, and human-in-the-loop AI where every result is reviewable and traceable. So far that has covered GIS and environmental workflows, civil engineering calculations, survey processing, and grant application scoring.

I usually end up in the hard parts of a company. Old code. Fragile flows. Systems no one wants to touch. I can step into a codebase I’ve never seen, trace it carefully, and come back with a fix that doesn’t destabilize everything else. It’s rarely glamorous, but it’s effective.

I know C# deeply from years inside .NET, most recently a core banking platform at Data Center Inc. — ACH processing, reconciliation, and incidents where real money is on the line. Before that, ten years at S&P Global on real-time financial data for institutional clients. Given the choice I prefer frontend engineering; complex UI state and performance problems are usually just puzzles.

Outside of work I build my own products end to end. U-Mail.ai for email productivity, ApplyPro.ai for AI-assisted resumes, now past 400 active users. I own the design, the backend, the payments, and the 2am bug reports. Also, no one else is going to fix my bugs.
There’s a method to how I work. I don’t chase trends, I build things that hold up. If you need someone steady who can navigate complexity and turn ideas into working software, I’m happy to talk.

trilon.title: Applied AI Field Engineer
trilon.description: Work within a cross-functional team conducting onsite deep dives with engineering firms, documenting workflows, data sources, and calculations, then identifying where automation, AI, or purpose-built software delivers measurable value. Rapidly prototype full-stack applications: deterministic calculation, validation, and document cross-referencing tools, and human-in-the-loop AI workflows with reviewable results, citations, and traceability. Delivered environmental workflow automation over GIS and regulated modeling tools, civil engineering calculations for stormwater and hydrology, survey-data processing and coordinate transformation, and grant application scoring software. Write structured, reusable code and phased implementation plans so successful prototypes have a clear path to production.
